name: Schwarzschild Metric and Black Holes
equations: ds^2 = -\left(1 - \frac{2GM}{c^2 r}\right)c^2 dt^2 + \left(1 - \frac{2GM}{c^2 r}\right)^{-1}dr^2 + r^2(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta d\phi^2)
methods: Identify spherical vacuum symmetry outside a static non-rotating mass
Calculate proper time along static observer worldlines via metric coefficients
Compute gravitational redshift and frequency shifts near horizons
Determine effective potential for orbital motion and innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO)
problem_types: Gravitational redshift of signals from neutron stars and black holes
Precession of perihelion of Mercury via General Relativity geodesic equations
Light deflection angle past the solar limb
pitfalls: Treating Schwarzschild coordinate r as proper radial distance (dr is modified by metric factor)
Assuming coordinate time t matches proper time of an observer falling through the horizon
